gaps.sentence: I ___ hours yesterday trying to fix the printer, and it still doesn't work.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: to use time without any result
gaps.explanation: waste time means to spend time uselessly; the second clause shows there was no result.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ a diary since she was twelve.
gaps.explanation: keep a diary is the fixed collocation for writing in one regularly.

gaps.sentence: Let me ___ a photo of you both.
gaps.explanation: take a photo/picture is the fixed collocation for photographing something.

gaps.sentence: It ___ no difference whether we leave today or tomorrow.
gaps.explanation: 'Make no difference' is the fixed phrase.

gaps.sentence: Everyone agreed the suggestion was utterly ___.
gaps.explanation: utterly ridiculous is the standard collocation; 'utterly' is used with extreme adjectives.

gaps.sentence: He didn't ___ any interest in politics until university.
gaps.explanation: take an interest in something means to become curious or involved in it.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: There was ___ fog at the airport all morning.
gaps.explanation: thick fog (or dense fog) is the standard collocation; 'strong fog' is wrong.
